The process described involves B cells proliferating in Peyer's patches (secondary lymphoid organs in the intestine) after oral antigen delivery. Sequencing their variable heavy chain genes reveals high variability. This variability arises from somatic hypermutation, a process that introduces point mutations in the variable regions of immunoglobulin genes during the germinal center reaction, leading to affinity maturation. VDJ recombination occurs earlier in B cell development in the bone marrow and generates the primary repertoire, not the ongoing variability seen in activated peripheral B cells. Class switching recombination alters the constant region, not the variable region. Complement activation is an innate immune mechanism unrelated to B cell gene variability.
